chapter: Becoming a player; Rene, Bunk and Armstrong
title: Rene Petit and Bunk Johnson
summary: He tried to play with Rene's blues in C sharp and played with Bunk in Chicago in the 1940s.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: But what did you think about it? You said that René used to play the blues in these ladies?

Well René played in C Sharp. You mean C Sharp. C Sharp. Well that's the same thing. I sat in there with that, I grabbed the trumbo one night, Morrissey here and played with him. And I was feeling around him, you know. You were trying to find the trumbo? Feeling all around, trying to find the key. It was damn near old when I found the key, you understand what I'm talking about. Because I hadn't been used to playing.
Did you think René was a very good trumbo player?

Oh, I know he was. It was too bad he didn't do any recording them out there, and Buddy too. Buddy was on the art of Bunk. Now I played with Bunk in Chicago. Oh yeah? Yeah, Bunk, the central Bunk. The later years in the 40's now. Yeah, Bunk came up, but I could still see why they were talking about he was so great and he had taught Lil Armstrong during that time. But Bunk, every train they went there, they went to the station looking for Bunk to arrive, and he wouldn't be on that train. Finally, about the fourth train, the other Bunk, and they don't have no horn.
The horn might be on another train.

See they rediscovered him from New Ile Berry. He was in New Ile Berry, they were working. And so Bunk played that night, and George Brunus was there, and Paul Morales, and we had Brother McGrummers on the piano, and Lee Collins, he used Lee Collins on. We had Darnell Howard, and somebody else.
What did you think about Bunk playing then?
Well I could tell he wasn't very strong, but I could see why they raved over him.
